sn45.39:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you the spiritual path and the fruits of the spiritual path.

sn45.39:1.4.eng: And what is the spiritual path?

sn45.39:1.5.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.39:1.6.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.39:1.7.eng: This is called the spiritual path.

sn45.39:1.8.eng: And what are the fruits of the spiritual path?

sn45.39:1.9.eng: The fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

sn45.39:1.10.eng: These are called the fruits of the spiritual path.”

sn45.4:1.2.pli: Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
sn45.4:1.2.eng: Then Venerable Ānanda robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

sn45.4:1.3.pli: Addasā kho āyasmā ānando jāṇussoṇiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathena sāvatthiyā niyyāyantaṃ.
sn45.4:1.3.eng: He saw the brahmin Jānussoṇi driving out of Sāvatthī in an all-white chariot drawn by mares.
sn45.4:1.3.comm: For Jānussoṇi, see SN 12.47:1.2 and note. | A chariot drawn by mares was the preferred vehicle of Jānussoṇi (MN 99:30.1, MN 27:2.1), as well as the brahmin student Ambaṭṭha DN 3:1.6.1. Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.2.1 depicts Jānaśruti’s wealth as including cows, gold, and a chariot drawn by mules.

sn45.4:1.4.pli: Setā sudaṃ assā yuttā honti setālaṅkārā, seto ratho, setaparivāro, setā rasmiyo, setā patodalaṭṭhi, setaṃ chattaṃ, setaṃ uṇhīsaṃ, setāni vatthāni, setā upāhanā, setāya sudaṃ vālabījaniyā bījīyati.
sn45.4:1.4.eng: The yoked horses were pure white, as were the ornaments, chariot, upholstery, reins, goad, and canopy. And his turban, robes, sandals were white, as was the chowry fanning him.

sn45.4:1.5.eng: When people saw it they exclaimed,

sn45.4:1.7.eng: It’s a vehicle fit for divinity!”

sn45.4:2.1.pli: Atha kho āyasmā ānando sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca:
sn45.4:2.1.eng: Then Ānanda wandered for alms in Sāvatthī. After the meal, on his return from almsround, he went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened, adding,

sn45.4:3.1.pli: “Idhāhaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ.

sn45.4:3.2.pli: Addasaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, jāṇussoṇiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathena sāvatthiyā niyyāyantaṃ.

sn45.4:3.3.pli: Setā sudaṃ assā yuttā honti setālaṅkārā, seto ratho, setaparivāro, setā rasmiyo, setā patodalaṭṭhi, setaṃ chattaṃ, setaṃ uṇhīsaṃ, setāni vatthāni, setā upāhanā, setāya sudaṃ vālabījaniyā bījīyati.

sn45.4:3.7.pli: Sakkā nu kho, bhante, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye brahmayānaṃ paññāpetun”ti?
sn45.4:3.7.eng: “Sir, can you point out a divine vehicle in this teaching and training?”

sn45.4:4.2.pli: “imasseva kho etaṃ, ānanda, ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa adhivacanaṃ:
sn45.4:4.2.eng: “These are all terms for the noble eightfold path:

sn45.4:4.3.eng: ‘divine vehicle’, or else ‘vehicle of truth’, or else ‘supreme victory in battle’.

sn45.4:5.1.pli: Sammādiṭṭhi, ānanda, bhāvitā bahulīkatā rāgavinayapariyosānā hoti, dosavinayapariyosānā hoti, mohavinayapariyosānā hoti.
sn45.4:5.1.eng: When right view is developed and cultivated it culminates with the removal of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.4:5.2.pli: Sammāsaṅkappo, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno hoti, dosavinayapariyosāno hoti, mohavinayapariyosāno hoti.

sn45.4:5.3.pli: Sammāvācā, ānanda, bhāvitā bahulīkatā rāgavinayapariyosānā hoti, dosa …pe… mohavinayapariyosānā hoti.

sn45.4:5.4.pli: Sammākammanto, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno hoti, dosa …pe… mohavinayapariyosāno hoti.

sn45.4:5.5.pli: Sammāājīvo, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno hoti, dosa …pe… mohavinayapariyosāno hoti.

sn45.4:5.6.pli: Sammāvāyāmo, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno hoti, dosa …pe… mohavinayapariyosāno hoti.

sn45.4:5.7.pli: Sammāsati, ānanda, bhāvitā bahulīkatā rāgavinayapariyosānā hoti, dosa …pe… mohavinayapariyosānā hoti.

sn45.4:5.8.pli: Sammāsamādhi, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno hoti, dosa …pe… mohavinayapariyosāno hoti.
sn45.4:5.8.eng: right immersion is developed and cultivated it culminates with the removal of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.4:6.1.pli: Iminā kho etaṃ, ānanda, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā imassevetaṃ ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa adhivacanaṃ:
sn45.4:6.1.eng: This is a way to understand how these are all terms for the noble eightfold path:

sn45.4:6.2.eng: ‘divine vehicle’, or else ‘vehicle of truth’, or else ‘supreme victory in battle’.”

sn45.4:6.3.eng: That is what the Buddha said.

sn45.4:7.1.pli: Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā:
sn45.4:7.1.eng: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
sn45.4:7.1.comm: Verses connecting parts of the Dhamma to a chariot are also found at SN 1.46 and SN 41.5.

sn45.4:8.1.eng: “Of which the qualities of faith and wisdom
sn45.4:8.1.comm: The yassa (“of which …”) with which the verses open is not answered until etad (“this”) in the final verse. This creates a suspension over the entire text, like an unresolved note in a chord sequence. The suspense is further heightened by the absence of active verbs, drawing out the moment when movement finally starts; and it is literal movement, as the chariot “rolls” right into the resolution of “this” in the final verse. Only then is the true nature of the “divine vehicle” revealed. Such elaborate literary conceits, rare in the Suttas, are common in the Vedas. It is employed here to evoke the sophistication of Vedic verse, paralleling the luxury of the chariot. While I normally do not attempt to mimic Pali syntax so literally, here I feel the poetic effect is dramatic enough that it’s worth trying.

sn45.4:8.2.eng: are always yoked to the shaft;

sn45.4:8.3.eng: conscience its draft-pole, mind its strap,
sn45.4:8.3.comm: It is not easy to differentiate the dhura (“shaft”) from the īsā (“draft-pole”). The īsā is like the tusks of an elephant (MN 61.7.1, Ud 6.4:24.2), a forepart that might collide (SN 11.6:2.2), and which a colt might shake off (AN 8.14:12.4). Certain ancient images, such as the Indus Valley Daimabad toy chariot, clearly show a second part, a thicker “shaft” with a cylindrical end into which the draft-pole was fitted, which is perhaps the load-bearing dhura.

sn45.4:9.1.comm: Here at the start of the second verse is a partial resolution as the subject, left implicit in the first verse, is revealed.

sn45.4:9.2.eng: its axle absorption, energy its wheel;

sn45.4:9.3.comm: The Chinese parallel at SA 769 is helpful: 捨三昧為轅.

sn45.4:10.3.comm: As the soma “endures” the blows of the pressing stone (Rig Veda 2.13.3).

sn45.4:10.4.eng: to sanctuary from the yoke it rolls—

sn45.4:11.1.comm: The text plays with Vedic expressions, but the intent is purely Buddhist—the path rolls onwards due to one’s own practice.

sn45.4:11.3.eng: The attentive leave the world in it,

sn45.40:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you the spiritual path and the goal of the spiritual path.

sn45.40:1.4.eng: And what is the spiritual path?

sn45.40:1.5.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.40:1.6.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.40:1.7.eng: This is called the spiritual path.

sn45.40:1.8.eng: And what is the goal of the spiritual path?

sn45.40:1.9.pli: Yo kho, bhikkhave, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo—
sn45.40:1.9.eng: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.40:1.10.eng: This is called the goal of the spiritual path.”

sn45.41:0.2.eng: 5. Abbreviated Texts on Followers of Other Religions

sn45.41:1.2.pli: “Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ:
sn45.41:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, if wanderers who follow another religion were to ask you:

sn45.41:1.3.pli: ‘kimatthiyaṃ, āvuso, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha:
sn45.41:1.3.eng: ‘Reverends, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.41:1.4.eng: ‘The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is the fading away of greed.’

sn45.41:1.5.pli: Sace pana vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ:
sn45.41:1.5.eng: If wanderers of other religions were to ask you:

sn45.41:1.6.pli: ‘atthi panāvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā rāgavirāgāyā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha:
sn45.41:1.6.eng: ‘Is there a path and a practice for the fading away of greed?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.41:1.7.pli: ‘atthi kho, āvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā rāgavirāgāyā’ti.
sn45.41:1.7.eng: ‘There is a path and a practice for the fading away of greed.’

sn45.41:1.8.pli: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo, katamā ca paṭipadā rāgavirāgāya?
sn45.41:1.8.eng: And what is that path, what is that practice for the fading away of greed?

sn45.41:1.9.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.41:1.10.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.41:1.11.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo, ayaṃ paṭipadā rāgavirāgāyāti.
sn45.41:1.11.eng: This is the path, this is the practice for the fading away of greed.

sn45.41:1.12.pli: Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā”ti.
sn45.41:1.12.eng: When questioned by wanderers of other religions, that’s how you should answer them.”

sn45.42-47:0.2.eng: 5. Abbreviated Texts on Followers of Other Religions

sn45.42-47:0.3.eng: Six Discourses on Giving Up Fetters, Etc.

sn45.42-47:1.1.pli: “Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ:
sn45.42-47:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, if wanderers who follow another religion were to ask you:

sn45.42-47:1.2.pli: ‘kimatthiyaṃ, āvuso, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha:
sn45.42-47:1.2.eng: ‘Reverends, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.42-47:1.3.eng: ‘The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to give up the fetters.’ …

sn45.42-47:1.5.eng: ‘… to completely understand the course of time.’ …
sn45.42-47:1.5.comm: Addhāna (“course of time”) is a word for “transmigration” (saṁsāra), usually expressed as the “past (course)” and “future (course)” (SN 12.20:5.2). It is rooted in the metaphor of a journey, especially the long, dark road of the stars, sun and moon in the sky (eg. Rig Veda 1.113.3, 6.12.3, 6.29.2). Contrast the “first beginning” and “final end” (MN 79:7.5).

sn45.42-47:1.6.pli: ‘āsavānaṃ khayatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti …pe…

sn45.42-47:1.7.eng: ‘… to realize the fruit of knowledge and freedom.’ …

sn45.48:0.2.eng: 5. Abbreviated Texts on Followers of Other Religions

sn45.48:0.3.eng: Extinguishment With No Fuel For Grasping

sn45.48:1.2.pli: “Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ:
sn45.48:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, if wanderers who follow another religion were to ask you:

sn45.48:1.3.pli: ‘kimatthiyaṃ, āvuso, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha:
sn45.48:1.3.eng: ‘Reverends, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.48:1.4.eng: ‘The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.’

sn45.48:1.5.pli: Sace pana vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ:
sn45.48:1.5.eng: If wanderers of other religions were to ask you:

sn45.48:1.6.pli: ‘atthi panāvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā anupādāparinibbānāyā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha:
sn45.48:1.6.eng: ‘Is there a path and a practice for complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.48:1.7.pli: ‘atthi kho, āvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā anupādāparinibbānāyā’ti.
sn45.48:1.7.eng: ‘There is a path and a practice for complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.’

sn45.48:1.8.pli: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo, katamā ca paṭipadā anupādāparinibbānāya?
sn45.48:1.8.eng: And what is that path, what is that practice for complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping?

sn45.48:1.9.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.48:1.10.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.48:1.11.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo, ayaṃ paṭipadā anupādāparinibbānāyāti.
sn45.48:1.11.eng: This is the path, this is the practice for complete extinguishment with no fuel for grasping.

sn45.48:1.12.pli: Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā”ti.
sn45.48:1.12.eng: When questioned by wanderers of other religions, that’s how you should answer them.”

sn45.49:1.2.pli: “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—aruṇuggaṃ;
sn45.49:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise.

sn45.49:1.3.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—kalyāṇamittatā.
sn45.49:1.3.eng: In the same way good friendship is the forerunner and harbinger of the noble eightfold path for a mendicant.

sn45.49:1.4.pli: Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ—ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati.
sn45.49:1.4.eng: A mendicant with good friends can expect to develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path.

sn45.49:1.5.pli: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti?
sn45.49:1.5.eng: And how does a mendicant with good friends develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path?

sn45.49:1.6.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ …pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.
sn45.49:1.6.eng: It’s when a mendicant develops right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn45.49:1.7.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.
sn45.49:1.7.eng: That’s how a mendicant with good friends develops and cultivates the noble eightfold path.”

sn45.5:1.2.pli: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu …pe… ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ:
sn45.5:1.2.eng: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha … and said to him:

sn45.5:2.1.pli: “Idha no, bhante, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā amhe evaṃ pucchanti:
sn45.5:2.1.eng: “Sir, sometimes wanderers of other religions ask us:

sn45.5:2.2.eng: ‘Reverends, what’s the goal of leading the spiritual life under the ascetic Gotama?’

sn45.5:2.3.pli: Evaṃ puṭṭhā mayaṃ, bhante, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākaroma:

sn45.5:2.4.pli: ‘dukkhassa kho, āvuso, pariññatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti.
sn45.5:2.4.eng: ‘The goal of leading the spiritual life under the Buddha is to completely understand suffering.’
sn45.5:2.4.comm: One of the four functions regarding the four noble truths (SN 56.12:1.2, SN 56.29:1.5.

sn45.5:2.5.pli: Kacci mayaṃ, bhante, evaṃ puṭṭhā evaṃ byākaramānā vuttavādino ceva bhagavato homa, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhāma, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaroma, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī”ti?
sn45.5:2.5.eng: Answering this way, we trust that we repeat what the Buddha has said, and don’t misrepresent him with an untruth. We trust our explanation is in line with the teaching, and that there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.”

sn45.5:3.1.pli: “Taggha tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ puṭṭhā evaṃ byākaramānā vuttavādino ceva me hotha, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhatha, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākarotha, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati.
sn45.5:3.1.eng: “Indeed, in answering this way you repeat what I’ve said, and don’t misrepresent me with an untruth. Your explanation is in line with the teaching, and there are no legitimate grounds for rebuttal or criticism.

sn45.5:3.2.pli: Dukkhassa hi pariññatthaṃ mayi brahmacariyaṃ vussati.
sn45.5:3.2.eng: For the goal of leading the spiritual life under me is to completely understand suffering.

sn45.5:3.3.pli: Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ:
sn45.5:3.3.eng: If wanderers of other religions were to ask you:

sn45.5:3.4.pli: ‘atthi panāvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha:
sn45.5:3.4.eng: ‘Is there a path and a practice for completely understanding that suffering?’ You should answer them like this:

sn45.5:3.5.pli: ‘atthi kho, āvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyā’ti.

sn45.5:4.1.pli: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo, katamā paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyāti?

sn45.5:4.2.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.5:4.3.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.5:4.4.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo, ayaṃ paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyāti.
sn45.5:4.4.eng: This is the path and the practice for completely understanding suffering.

sn45.5:4.5.pli: Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā”ti.
sn45.5:4.5.eng: When questioned by wanderers of other religions, that’s how you should answer them.”

sn45.50-54:0.3.eng: Five Discourses on Accomplishment in Ethics, Etc. (1st)

sn45.50-54:1.1.pli: “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—aruṇuggaṃ;
sn45.50-54:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise.

sn45.50-54:1.2.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—sīlasampadā.
sn45.50-54:1.2.eng: In the same way accomplishment in ethics is the forerunner and harbinger of the arising of the noble eightfold path for a mendicant.

sn45.50-54:1.3.eng: A mendicant accomplished in ethics can expect to develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path. …” …

sn45.50-54:1.4.comm: “Enthusiasm” (chanda) is the desire to achieve the wholesome, especially liberation from transmigration. It is one of the bases of psychic power (SN 51).

sn45.50-54:1.5.comm: “Accomplishment in self-development” (attasampadā) is found only here and in parallel passages. In similar contexts we find cittasampadā (“accomplishment in mental development”), i.e. samādhi (AN 3.117:4.3). Hence the commentary glosses attā with citta here.

sn45.50-54:1.6.comm: Normally one “accomplished in view” is a stream-enterer (SN 13.10:3.1).

sn45.55:0.3.eng: Accomplishment in Rational Application of Mind (1st)

sn45.55:1.1.pli: “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—aruṇuggaṃ;
sn45.55:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise.

sn45.55:1.2.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—yonisomanasikārasampadā.
sn45.55:1.2.eng: In the same way accomplishment in rational application of mind is the forerunner and harbinger of the noble eightfold path for a mendicant.

sn45.55:1.3.pli: Yonisomanasikārasampannassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ—ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati.
sn45.55:1.3.eng: A mendicant accomplished in rational application of mind can expect to develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path.

sn45.55:1.4.pli: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti?
sn45.55:1.4.eng: And how does a mendicant accomplished in rational application of mind develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path?

sn45.55:1.5.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ …pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.
sn45.55:1.5.eng: It’s when a mendicant develops right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn45.55:1.6.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.
sn45.55:1.6.eng: That’s how a mendicant accomplished in rational application of mind develops and cultivates the noble eightfold path.”

sn45.56:1.1.pli: “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—aruṇuggaṃ;
sn45.56:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise.

sn45.56:1.2.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—kalyāṇamittatā.
sn45.56:1.2.eng: In the same way good friendship is the forerunner and harbinger of the noble eightfold path for a mendicant.

sn45.56:1.3.pli: Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ—ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati.
sn45.56:1.3.eng: A mendicant with good friends can expect to develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path.

sn45.56:1.4.pli: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti?
sn45.56:1.4.eng: And how does a mendicant with good friends develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path?

sn45.56:1.5.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ …pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ.
sn45.56:1.5.eng: It’s when a mendicant develops right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion, which culminate in the removal of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.56:1.6.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.
sn45.56:1.6.eng: That’s how a mendicant with good friends develops and cultivates the noble eightfold path.”

sn45.57-61:0.3.eng: Five Discourses on Accomplishment in Ethics, Etc. (2nd)

sn45.57-61:1.1.pli: “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—aruṇuggaṃ;
sn45.57-61:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise.

sn45.57-61:1.2.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ—sīlasampadā …pe…
sn45.57-61:1.2.eng: In the same way accomplishment in ethics is the forerunner and harbinger of the noble eightfold path for a mendicant. …”

sn45.6:1.2.pli: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca:
sn45.6:1.2.eng: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

sn45.6:1.3.eng: “Sir, they speak of this thing called the ‘spiritual path’.

sn45.6:1.4.pli: Katamaṃ nu kho, bhante, brahmacariyaṃ, katamaṃ brahmacariyapariyosānan”ti?
sn45.6:1.4.eng: What is the spiritual path? And what is the culmination of the spiritual path?”

sn45.6:2.1.pli: “Ayameva kho, bhikkhu, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo brahmacariyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ—
sn45.6:2.1.eng: “Mendicant, the spiritual path is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.6:2.2.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.6:2.3.pli: Yo kho, bhikkhu, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo—
sn45.6:2.3.eng: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.6:2.4.eng: This is the culmination of the spiritual path.”
